To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the presence of heterospecific serum in primary cultures is necessary and sufficient for the generation of H-2- but not non-H-2-restriction in secondary MLC and that this phenomenon is unrelated to the presence or absence of non-H- 2 alloantigeneic stimuli in the primary cultures.
secondary in vitro responses of Mls locus-primed T lymphocytes to Mls locus antigents are not dependent on the presence of the primary-stimulating alloantigens.
secondary in vitro responses of Mls locus-primed T lymphocytes to H-2 alloantigenic determinants are not dependent on Mls locus products.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of non-H2 alloantigents, particularly Mls locus antigents, in secondary in-vitro T-cell-mediated responses.
the role of non-H2 alloantigems, specifically Mls- locus products, in the generation of secondary in vitro T lymphocyte-mediated cytotoxic responses.
the role of non-H2 alloantigems, specifically Mls products, in secondary T-cell-mediated cytolytic responses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Mls locus antigents, as primary-stimulating alloantigens of T lymphocytes, are not required for the induction of secondary, self- H-2-restrictive T cell responses in MLC or CML.
non-H-2 locus alloantigencies, in particular Mls locus products (which are not H-2-associated), are not required for secondary in vitro T-lymphocyte responses to H-2-associated structures.
the secondary in vitro reactivity of activated Mls locus-primed T lymphocytes is not dependent upon the presence of the original Mls locus-activating antigen(s).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

non-H-2-activated T-cell clones are not capable of developing secondary in vitro responses against non-H-2 antigens, and that the development of such responses is dependent on the primary culture serum environment.
Mls locus antigems do not participate in the generation of secondary in vitro T cell responses.
the presence or absence of Mls locus alloreactivity in secondary responses of T lymphocyte clones depends on whether the clones were activated against Mls products in the primary culture or not.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of heteroantibodies in the culture medium is a necessary and sufficient condition for development of H2-restricted responses.
the presence of hetero- serum during the primary culture phase can influence the nature of secondary in vitro responses of alloactivated T lymphocytes.
the Mls locus antigems are not required for the development of H- 2-restricted responses.
